items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> at the point where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}</annotation></semantics></math>, upside down. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math>: the vertical rate over the horizontal rate.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> alone, how fast <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> changes per unit of time. Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 9</annotation></semantics></math> to get the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> per unit of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Write an equation of the line tangent to the path at the point where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = \frac{-4}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>; this line uses the reciprocal.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>, a rate per unit of time. The slope of the line is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt} = -\frac{4}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The point is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x(2), y(2)) = (2, 0)</annotation></semantics></math>, so the line is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y - 0 = -\frac{4}{9}(x - 2)</annotation></semantics></math>: subtract 2.

items.q: Which statement describes the tangent line at the point where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = -1</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: It is horizontal, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 0</annotation></semantics></math> there

It has slope 2, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = 2</annotation></semantics></math> there

It is vertical, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math> there

It does not exist, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined there

items.q: Find the slope of the curve at the point where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That divides <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(3)</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(3)</annotation></semantics></math>. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{y'(3)}{x'(3)}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(3)</annotation></semantics></math> alone, a rate per unit of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide it by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(3) = -4</annotation></semantics></math>.

That divides the values <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(3)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(3)</annotation></semantics></math>; the slope uses the derivatives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(3)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(3)</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Write an equation of the line tangent to the curve at the point where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{y'(0)}{x'(0)} = \frac{-2}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>; this line uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x'(0)}{y'(0)}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The point is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x(0), y(0)) = (1, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>. The time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> is not the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate; use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x - 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Put the rate of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> on top: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2t}{e^t}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = e^t</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A curve is given by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3\cos t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2\sin t</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}</annotation></semantics></math>. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2\cos t}{-3\sin t}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos t</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\sin t</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = -3\sin t</annotation></semantics></math> and the slope is negative where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos t</annotation></semantics></math> are both positive.

expr.answerHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{-2\,\cos(t)}{3\,\sin(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>

options: It is 0, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 0)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A point moves along a curve. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That divides <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math>. The chain rule multiplies: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = \frac{dy}{dx}\cdot\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That divides the slope by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>. Multiply instead: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt} = 3t^2 - 12t</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}</annotation></semantics></math>, upside down. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, a rate per unit of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide it by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 2</annotation></semantics></math> once more.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The second derivative with respect to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> divided by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{3t^2 - 12t}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> already holds one division by 2; its <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>-derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3t - 6</annotation></semantics></math>, and one more division by 2 gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3t - 6}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For which values of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> is the curve concave up?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 2</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 < t < 5</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 4</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 < t < 5</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: At which point does the curve have a point of inflection?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(5, -16)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, -16)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>32</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(9, -32)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 0)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That multiplies by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{1}{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. Dividing by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{t}</annotation></semantics></math> multiplies by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2t - 4}{1/t}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= t(2t - 4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> alone. Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{1}{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}(2t^2 - 4t) = 4t - 4</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> as well.

That divides <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = 2</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -\frac{1}{t^2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The formula is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>÷</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) \div \frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dt^2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the second derivative with respect to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. What does the second derivative tell you about the point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\ln 2, -4)</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> has a relative maximum there, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} > 0</annotation></semantics></math>

It is a point of inflection, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> has a relative minimum there, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} > 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Nothing, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math> there

items.q: A curve is given by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = t^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = t^3</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t > 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{3t}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 2t</annotation></semantics></math> once more.

That divides <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dt^2} = 6t</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, then divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>.
