What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2e^t</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4e^t</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2e^{-t}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: The circle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \cos t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin t</annotation></semantics></math> has <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{\cos t}{\sin t}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>csc</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(-\cot t\right) = \csc^2 t</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = -\sin t = -\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The sign: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = -\sin t</annotation></semantics></math>, so dividing <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>csc</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc^2 t</annotation></semantics></math> by it gives a negative number. The point is on the upper half, which is concave down.

items.q: For a curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = x(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = y(t)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which expression equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y/dt^2}{d^2x/dt^2}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/dx}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: For a curve, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = t + 1</annotation></semantics></math> and the slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = t\sin(t^2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(t\sin(t^2)\right)</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1.5</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide it by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 2.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A curve is given by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = t^3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = t^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Which describes its concavity?
options: Concave down for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t < 0</annotation></semantics></math> and for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t > 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Concave up for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t < 0</annotation></semantics></math> and for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t > 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Concave up for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, concave down for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t < 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Concave down for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, concave up for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t < 0</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, a curve has <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = -2</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, a rate per unit of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt} = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

That multiplies by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math>. To change a rate per unit of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> into a rate per unit of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, divide.

items.q: Which integral gives the length of one arch?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{2\pi} \sqrt{(t - \sin t)^2 + (1 - \cos t)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{2\pi} \sqrt{(1 - \cos t)^2 + (\sin t)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{2\pi} \left((1 - \cos t) + \sin t\right)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{2\pi} \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{\sin t}{1 - \cos t}\right)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: At the top of the arch, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(x'(\pi))^2 + (y'(\pi))^2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the speed of the rim point there.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x'(\pi))^2 + (y'(\pi))^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2^2 + 0^2</annotation></semantics></math>. Take the square root.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(\pi) = \sin\pi</annotation></semantics></math> alone. The point still moves sideways: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(\pi) = 1 - \cos\pi = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Using <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1 - \cos t)^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \sin^2 t</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 - 2\cos t</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 4\sin^2\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, find the exact length of one arch.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is the length of the arch's base, the straight distance the wheel rolls. The arch itself is longer: integrate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> from 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

An antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4\cos\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>: the inside derivative <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> doubles the factor.

items.q: The wheel keeps rolling, and the rim point traces the path for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. How long is the path it traces?

mistakes.why: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 4\pi</annotation></semantics></math> the point traces two arches, each of length 8; the integral over <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 4\pi]</annotation></semantics></math> counts both.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is how far the wheel rolls along the axis; the curved path above it is longer.

items.q: Find the speed of the drone at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math> seconds. Include units.

mistakes.why: That adds the components, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 + 12</annotation></semantics></math>. Speed is the length of the velocity: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{5^2 + 12^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^2 + 12^2</annotation></semantics></math>; take the square root.

items.q: Which expression gives the length of the drone's path from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 \left(x'(t) + y'(t)\right)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\left(\int_0^4 x'(t)\,dt\right)^2 + \left(\int_0^4 y'(t)\,dt\right)^2}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}\right)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Use a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals given by the table to approximate the length of the drone's path from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>. Include units.

mistakes.why: The subintervals are not equal: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 3]</annotation></semantics></math> has width 2. Multiply each average speed by its own width.

That is a left Riemann sum, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>13</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5(1) + 10(2) + 13(1)</annotation></semantics></math>. A trapezoid averages the speeds at both ends of each subinterval.

items.q: What does the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math> represent?
options: The distance, in meters, between the drone's positions at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>

The drone's average speed, in meters per second, from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>

The distance, in meters, that the drone travels along its path from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>
The drone's height, in meters, at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the length of the curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = e^t\cos t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = e^t\sin t</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x')^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ (y')^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= e^{2t}\left[(\cos t - \sin t)^2 + (\sin t + \cos t)^2\right]</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2e^{2t}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the integrand is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2}\,e^t</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^t</annotation></semantics></math>.

Evaluate at both limits: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2}\,e^t\Big|_0^1 = \sqrt{2}(e - 1)</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0.

items.q: Find the length of the path <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1 + 3t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2 - 4t</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|3| + |-4|</annotation></semantics></math> before multiplying by 2. The speed is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{3^2 + (-4)^2} = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

5 is the speed, the length covered per unit of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Over 2 units of time the length is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 \cdot 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the length of the curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \cos^3 t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin^3 t</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{\pi/2} 3\sin t\cos t\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{3}{2}\sin^2 t\Big|_0^{\pi/2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin t\cos t</annotation></semantics></math> has the factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x')^2 + (y')^2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 9\sin^2 t\cos^2 t</annotation></semantics></math>, and its square root is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\sin t\cos t</annotation></semantics></math>: take the root of the 9 as well.

items.q: Find the length of the curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = t^2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{2}{3}t^3</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le \sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{4t^2 + 4t^4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2t\sqrt{1 + t^2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the factor 2 comes out of the root as well.

With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = 1 + t^2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = 2t\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int 2t\sqrt{1 + t^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \int u^{1/2}\,du</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2}{3}u^{3/2}</annotation></semantics></math>; there is no extra factor 2.

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \cos(2t)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin(2t)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, the integral <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{2\pi} \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math> equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. Which statement is correct?
options: The circle has circumference <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, so its radius is 2

The point goes around the unit circle twice, so the integral is twice the circumference <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>

The integral should be <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>; a value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math> means an arithmetic slip
The integral measures the area inside the circle, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the length of the curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = t^3 - t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = t^2</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the straight-line distance from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(6, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>. The curve bends, so integrate the speed: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^2 \sqrt{(3t^2 - 1)^2 + (2t)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le 1</annotation></semantics></math>, can be written as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = t</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = t^2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le t \le 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Which integral gives its length?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \sqrt{1 + 2t}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \sqrt{t^2 + t^4}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \sqrt{1 + 4t^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 (1 + 2t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Use the data in the table to estimate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Include units.

mistakes.why: That is the change <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(3) - x(1)</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by the time it took, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 - 1 = 2</annotation></semantics></math> seconds.

That is the average rate from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>. Use the two times closest to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> on either side: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which vector is the best estimate of the robot's velocity vector at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, in meters per second?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 6, -4 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 5, 2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -2, 3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 3, -2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Use your estimate of the velocity vector at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> to estimate the robot's speed at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, in meters per second.

mistakes.why: That adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 + 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{3^2 + (-2)^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^2 + (-2)^2</annotation></semantics></math>; take the square root.

A negative component still adds to the speed: square it, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2)^2 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Based on the table, in which direction is the robot most likely moving at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 5</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Right and up
Right and down
Left and up
Left and down

options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -2, 3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -3, 2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 0, -2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 3, 2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the acceleration vector at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -3, 2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 6, -2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 0, -2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 0, 2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: At what time is the particle at rest?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the slope of the particle's path at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x'(3)}{y'(3)}</annotation></semantics></math>. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{y'(3)}{x'(3)}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(3)</annotation></semantics></math> alone. Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'(3) = 27 - 18 = 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

Straight to the right
Up and to the left

items.q: If <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\langle t^3 - 2t, e^{2t} \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, what is the velocity vector at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math>?

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\langle \sin(3t), t^4 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, find the horizontal component of the acceleration vector, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x''(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\cos(3t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -3\sin(3t)</annotation></semantics></math>: the derivative of cosine brings a minus sign.

The chain rule applies at each derivative: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x' = 3\cos(3t)</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x'' = 3 \cdot (-3\sin(3t))</annotation></semantics></math>.

Each derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(3t)</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(3t)</annotation></semantics></math> brings a factor 3 from the chain rule: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 \cdot 3 = 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

expr.answerHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>9</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-9\,\sin(3t)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>t</mi></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\langle \sqrt{t}, \ln(t^2 + 1) \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, find the vertical component of the velocity vector, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y'(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: By the chain rule, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mi>u</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\ln(u) = \frac{u'}{u}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = t^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the numerator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u' = 2t</annotation></semantics></math>.

The derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln u</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mi>u</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{u'}{u}</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> in the denominator.

items.q: A particle has position <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\langle 2t, t^2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. Find its speed at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That adds the components of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(2) = \left\langle 2, 4 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. Speed is its magnitude, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2^2 + 4^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^2 + 4^2</annotation></semantics></math>; take the square root.

That is the length of the position <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(2) = \left\langle 4, 4 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. Speed uses the velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the magnitude of the position <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(1.2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Include the vertical component <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}e^{t/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals in the table to approximate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(8)</annotation></semantics></math>, the boat's <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 8</annotation></semantics></math>. Include units.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>8</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^8 x'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Add the starting value: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(8)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>8</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^8 x'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>26.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 26.5</annotation></semantics></math>.

The starting value is added, not subtracted: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(8)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>8</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^8 x'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use a left Riemann sum with the three subintervals in the table to approximate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(8)</annotation></semantics></math>, the boat's <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 8</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>. Add the starting value <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = -1</annotation></semantics></math>.

The starting value is added: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(8)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= y(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>8</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^8 y'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ (-4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

That uses right endpoints: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2)(2) + 0(3) + 5(3)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>11</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 11</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>. A left sum takes each subinterval's left value.

items.q: Find the vertical component of the position, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> this gives 0, but <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 4</annotation></semantics></math>: add the initial position's vertical component.

The initial value is added: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= y(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^t (3 - 3s^2)\,ds</annotation></semantics></math>.

The vertical velocity is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 - 3t^2</annotation></semantics></math>, which includes the initial 3; its antiderivative has the term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3t</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the greatest value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3t - t^3</annotation></semantics></math>; the position also includes the initial height <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the starting height. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y' = 3 - 3t^2 > 0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so the particle rises before it falls.

items.q: A particle has velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(t) = \left\langle 6t^2, \cos t \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(0) = \left\langle 1, 2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>.
