mistakes.why: This has <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(0) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>; add the initial value <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(0) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

That differentiates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6t^2</annotation></semantics></math>. Position comes from antidifferentiating the velocity: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int 6t^2\,dt = 2t^3</annotation></semantics></math>.

The initial value is added: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^t 6s^2\,ds</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A particle has velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(t) = \left\langle 2t, \pi\cos(\pi t) \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(0) = \left\langle 1, 3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. Add <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^2 \sin(t^2)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>. Add <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(0) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

The initial value is added, not subtracted: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^2 \sin(t^2)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For the particle with velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>,</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left\langle \sqrt{t + 1}, \sin(t^2) \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(0) = \left\langle 2, 1 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(3)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly, without a calculator.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^3 \sqrt{t + 1}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Add <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(0) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The initial value is added: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>14</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(3) = 2 + \frac{14}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{3}(t + 1)^{3/2}</annotation></semantics></math> at the upper limit alone. Subtract its value at the lower limit too: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>14</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{3}(8 - 1) = \frac{14}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A particle starts at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(0) = \left\langle 1, 1 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 \mathbf{v}(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left\langle 5, -2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. Where is the particle at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 5, -2 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 6, -1 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -2, -1 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -2, 6 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 2, -1 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the speed of the particle at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{dy}{dx}\right| = \left|\frac{-1}{-2}\right|</annotation></semantics></math>, the steepness of the path. Speed is the length of the velocity vector, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That adds the sizes of the components. Speed is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(-2)^2 + (-1)^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2)^2 + (-1)^2</annotation></semantics></math>; take the square root.

items.q: Which statement about the motion from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = -2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math> is correct?
options: The displacement is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 0, 0 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, so the distance traveled is 0

The displacement is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 4, 0 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, the farthest point from the start

The displacement is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 3, -3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, the position at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>

The displacement is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle 0, 0 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>, but the distance traveled is positive

items.q: Which expression gives the total distance traveled by the particle from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = -2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{-2}^{2} \sqrt{(4 - t^2)^2 + (t^3 - 4t)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msqrt><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{-2}^{2} \sqrt{4t^2 + (3t^2 - 4)^2}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{\left(\int_{-2}^{2} -2t\,dt\right)^2 + \left(\int_{-2}^{2} (3t^2 - 4)\,dt\right)^2}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{-2}^{2} \left|\frac{3t^2 - 4}{-2t}\right|\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -2, 3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\langle -2, 6 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the speed of the particle at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{dy}{dx}\right|</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>. Speed is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(x'(2))^2 + (y'(2))^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the time <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 2</annotation></semantics></math> at which the speed of the particle is 3.

Find the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate of the particle's position at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^4 x'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>, the change in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Add the start: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(4)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x(0)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^4 x'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.

The starting value is added, not subtracted: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(4)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \int_0^4 x'(t)\,dt</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: In which direction is the particle moving at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Right and up
Left and down
Right and down
Left and up

items.q: Find the total distance traveled by the particle from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the length of the displacement vector, the straight-line distance from start to end. Distance traveled integrates the speed.

That integrates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|x'(t)| + |y'(t)|</annotation></semantics></math>. Speed combines the components with the Pythagorean theorem: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{(x')^2 + (y')^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A particle has position <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\langle t^2, t^3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. What is its speed at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>13</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{13}</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A particle moves with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x(t) = t^2 - 4t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y(t) = 12t - t^3</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 4</annotation></semantics></math>. On which interval is the particle's <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate decreasing?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 2</annotation></semantics></math>
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 < t < 4</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 < t < 4</annotation></semantics></math>
Nowhere on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < t < 4</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A particle moves with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\langle 3\cos t, 3\sin t \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. Find the total distance it travels from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the displacement: the particle returns to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 0)</annotation></semantics></math>. Distance integrates the speed, which is 3 the whole time.

The speed is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{9\sin^2 t + 9\cos^2 t} = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, not 9: take the square root.

items.q: A particle has velocity <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{v}(t) = \left\langle 3t^2, 3t \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>. Find the distance it travels from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = \sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>0</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t^2 + 1)^{3/2}\Big|_0^{\sqrt{3}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 8 - 1</annotation></semantics></math>: the lower limit gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1^{3/2} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0.

With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = t^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int 3t\sqrt{t^2 + 1}\,dt</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{3}{2}\int u^{1/2}\,du</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (t^2 + 1)^{3/2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the factors 3, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> cancel.

items.q: Particle A has position <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}_A(t) = \left\langle 2t, t^2 - 1 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> and particle B has position <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold">r</mi><mi>B</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{r}_B(t) = \left\langle t + 2, 3t - 3 \right\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \ge 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Do they collide, and if so, when and where?
options: Yes, at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, at the point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 3)</annotation></semantics></math>

Yes, at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(8, 15)</annotation></semantics></math>, where their paths cross

Yes, at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, where both have <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 0</annotation></semantics></math>
No, they do not collide

items.q: For a polar curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = f(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>, which expression is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(\theta)\cos\theta - f(\theta)\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(\theta)\sin\theta + f(\theta)\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-f'(\theta)\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(\theta)\cos\theta + f(\theta)\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the slope of the tangent line to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, the rate of change of the distance from the pole. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The fraction is upside down: the slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> on top.

items.q: For the spiral <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \theta</annotation></semantics></math>, write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. Write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>θ</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \theta\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>θ</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \theta\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and divide <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The fraction is upside down: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is the slope of the ray to the point, not of the curve; the product rule adds a second term to each derivative.

expr.answerHtml: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>θ</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sin(\theta) + \theta\,\cos(\theta)}{\cos(\theta) - \theta\,\sin(\theta)}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, is the point on the curve moving toward the pole or away from it, as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> increases?
options: Away from the pole: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 4</annotation></semantics></math> is large

Toward the pole: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} < 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Away from the pole: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta} < 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Neither: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0</annotation></semantics></math> makes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>, is the point on the curve moving toward the pole or away from it, as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> increases?
options: Away: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r < 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|r|</annotation></semantics></math> grows

Toward: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing
Toward: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r < 0</annotation></semantics></math> puts the point on the opposite ray
Neither: the point is at the pole

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = r\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{dr}{d\theta}\sin\theta + r\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

Only the first term, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, is 0 at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math>; the product rule adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\cos\theta = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> of the curve at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The fraction is upside down: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{-2}{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> (or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> alone). Divide <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta} = -4</annotation></semantics></math>.

Both derivatives are negative here, so their quotient is positive: check the sign of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta} = -r\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = -4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate of the point on the curve at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That would be <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 1</annotation></semantics></math> on the ray <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>. Here <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = -1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = (-1)(-1) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: At which points does a polar curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = f(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> have a horizontal tangent line?
options: Where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta} = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta} \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dx}{d\theta} = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta} \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>
Where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 0</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: The rose <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2\cos(3\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> passes through the pole at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find the slope of its tangent line there.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 0</annotation></semantics></math> there, but <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} = -6</annotation></semantics></math>, so neither derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> is 0. Compute both and divide.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, the rate of change of the distance. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The fraction is upside down: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{-3}{-3\sqrt{3}}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For a polar curve, which expression gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{d\theta}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dfrac{d^2y/d\theta^2}{d^2x/d\theta^2}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dfrac{\frac{d}{d\theta}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dfrac{d^2y/d\theta^2}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: For a polar curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = f(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(1) = -3</annotation></semantics></math>. What does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(1) = -3</annotation></semantics></math> mean?
options: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the slope of the curve is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-3</annotation></semantics></math>
The distance from the pole shrinks at 3 units per radian

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the point is moving downward at 3 units per radian
At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the point is 3 units from the pole

items.q: A point moves along <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2 + 2\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d\theta}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> radian per second. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{dt}</annotation></semantics></math> when <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. Multiply by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d\theta}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> to get the rate per second.

That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. It is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, is the point on the curve moving toward the pole or away from it, as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> increases?
options: Away: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.168</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(2) \approx 1.168</annotation></semantics></math> is positive, so the distance grows

Away: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.819</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} \approx -0.819</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos 2 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>

Toward: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta} < 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so the point drops

Toward: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.168</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(2) \approx 1.168 > 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.819</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} \approx -0.819 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the slope <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> of the curve at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The fraction is upside down: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy/d\theta}{dx/d\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The curve has a horizontal tangent line at one value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo><</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find that value.

mistakes.why: That solves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dr}{d\theta} = 1 - 2\sin\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, where the distance from the pole is largest. A horizontal tangent needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{d\theta} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the distance from the point on the curve at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 2.5</annotation></semantics></math> to the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, the distance from the pole. The distance from the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|r\cos\theta|</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|y| = |r\sin\theta|</annotation></semantics></math>, the distance from the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis.

items.q: Which integral gives the area of the shaded petal?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{\pi/2} 9\sin^2(2\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} 9\sin^2(2\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} 3\sin^2(2\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi} 9\sin^2(2\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the area of the shaded petal.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

That integrates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> instead of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} 3\sin(2\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{3}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Square <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> first.

items.q: Find the total area enclosed by all four petals of the rose.

mistakes.why: That is one petal. There are four, all the same size.

From 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> the curve traces only two of the petals; go to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, or multiply one petal by 4.

items.q: Why are the limits of integration for the shaded petal <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: The petal lies in the first quadrant, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is largest at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at both, so the petal starts and ends at the pole

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> has period <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, half of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the area of the part of the shaded petal with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the whole petal; the ray <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> cuts it in half.

That halves twice. Only one half of the petal is swept from 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the area of the region enclosed by the circle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 4\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: From 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> the circle is traced twice (for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo><</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi < \theta < 2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r < 0</annotation></semantics></math> retraces it). Integrate over <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

The diameter is 4, so the radius is 2, and the area is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>; check the setup <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi} 16\sin^2\theta\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the area of the region enclosed by the cardioid <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 1 - \sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

That integrates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{2\pi} (1 - \sin\theta)\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.
