items.q: Which expression gives the area inside the small inner loop of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 1 + 2\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{2\pi/3} (1 + 2\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{-2\pi/3}^{2\pi/3} (1 + 2\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{2\pi/3}^{4\pi/3} (1 + 2\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{2\pi} (1 + 2\cos\theta)^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the area of the region swept by the spiral <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 1 + \theta\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

That integrates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Why does a polar area integral have <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2</annotation></semantics></math> in it?
options: A thin wedge is nearly a circle slice, of area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2\,\Delta\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

It is the area of a thin rectangle of height <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> and width <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

It is the average of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2</annotation></semantics></math> over the interval
The curve is traced twice, so the area is halved

items.q: Find the area of the sector of the circle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the sector is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> must be squared: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}(2)^2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the area swept by the radius to the spiral <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>θ</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \sqrt{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> goes from 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{2\pi} \theta\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{(2\pi)^2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\pi^2</annotation></semantics></math>; then halve it once more for the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use a left Riemann sum with the three subintervals in the table to approximate the area swept from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} r^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the integrand is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}r^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the right sum, using <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. A left sum uses the left end of each subinterval.
<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is not squared: square each value before adding.

items.q: Use a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals in the table to approximate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} r^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That averages <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^2</annotation></semantics></math>. Square each value first.

items.q: What does <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_0^{\pi/2} r^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math> measure for this curve?
options: The length of the curve from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

The area between the curve and the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis, for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le x \le 3</annotation></semantics></math>

The average distance from the pole for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

The area swept by the radius from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A student approximates the area swept from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2.5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}(2 + 2.5 + 3.2)</annotation></semantics></math>. What is wrong?
options: The width should be <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the length of the interval

The values used should be <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.5</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>

The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and the squares of the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>-values are missing
A table gives no way to estimate a polar area

items.q: At which angles do the two circles cross?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Which integral gives the area of the shaded region, inside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 4\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and outside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{\pi/6}^{5\pi/6} \left(16\sin^2\theta - 4\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{\pi/6}^{5\pi/6} \left(4\sin\theta - 2\right)^2 d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{\pi/6}^{5\pi/6} \left(4 - 16\sin^2\theta\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\pi} \left(16\sin^2\theta - 4\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the area of the shaded region.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

That integrates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}(4\sin\theta - 2)^2</annotation></semantics></math>, squaring the difference. Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\left((4\sin\theta)^2 - 2^2\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

Check the sign of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(2\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> at the limits: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{5\pi}{3} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{3} - \sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= +4\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The disk <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r \le 4\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> has area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. Find the area of the region inside both circles.

mistakes.why: That is the shaded crescent itself. Subtract it from the whole disk, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

Subtract the whole crescent area, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4\pi}{3} + 2\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: How does the area inside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and outside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 4\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> compare with the area of the shaded region?
options: It is smaller: the circle <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math> is mostly inside the other
They are equal
It is larger: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math> is the bigger circle
It needs a new integral with new limits

items.q: Find the area of the region between the circles <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 3</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That squares the difference: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}(3 - 2)^2 \cdot \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Square each radius, then subtract.

That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

items.q: Find the area of the region inside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and outside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

That integrates from 0 to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, half the region. The region is symmetric about the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-axis: go from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, or double.

items.q: Why is the area between an outer curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = R(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> and an inner curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = r(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> equal to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int \left(R^2 - r^2\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int (R - r)^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Squaring a difference could give a negative number

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R - r)^2</annotation></semantics></math> is the same expression, multiplied out

Each thin piece is a big wedge minus a small wedge: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}R^2\,\Delta\theta - \frac{1}{2}r^2\,\Delta\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int (R - r)^2\,d\theta</annotation></semantics></math> counts the inner region twice

items.q: The limaçon <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 1 + 2\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> has an outer loop (area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi + \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>) and an inner loop (area <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi - \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>). Find the area of the region inside the outer loop and outside the inner loop.

mistakes.why: That adds the two loop areas. The inner loop is inside the outer one, so subtract it.

Subtracting <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math> terms add to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the area of the region inside both <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is half the region, the part with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>. The part from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, bounded by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, is the same size.

That is the whole disk inside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. The common region is only the lens where the two disks overlap.

items.q: At what value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le \pi</annotation></semantics></math> do the circle and the spiral meet?

mistakes.why: That is the common value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>. The question asks for the angle, where <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + \theta = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the area of the region inside the circle and outside the spiral for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le \theta \le 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

That integrates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\left(3 - (1 + \theta)\right)^2</annotation></semantics></math>, the square of the difference. Square each radius, then subtract.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the region inside the spiral and outside the circle for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \le \theta \le \pi</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_2^{\pi} \left(9 - (1 + \theta)^2\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_2^{\pi} \left((1 + \theta)^2 - 9\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\int_2^{\pi} \left(\theta - 2\right)^2 d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>θ</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_2^{\pi} \left((1 + \theta)^2 - 9\right)d\theta</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the area of the region inside the spiral and outside the circle for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \le \theta \le \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That leaves out the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in front of the integral.

That integrates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}(\theta - 2)^2</annotation></semantics></math>, the square of the difference of the radii.

items.q: The curves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = \cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> both pass through the pole, but solving <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta = \cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> gives only <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>. Why?
options: The pole is not a point of either curve

Equal <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> at equal <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is the one way two curves can meet

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{5\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> also solves it, at the pole

They reach the pole at different angles: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>
